subject.title: [Bug]: Non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text '[tool: exec]' instead of tool_use blocks

question: How should OpenClaw handle a bare model-emitted tool marker such as `[tool: exec]` when no arguments or structured tool call are present?
rationale: The source can identify the bad shape, but execution cannot be safely reconstructed without deciding runtime policy for retry, fallback, user-visible warning, or provider blocking.

options.title: Detect and recover without execution
options.body: Treat bare markers as malformed tool intent, suppress the raw marker, and retry or fall through to a tool-capable model with a clear diagnostic.

options.title: Warn and stop the turn
options.body: Hide the raw marker and tell the user/operator that the selected model cannot produce a valid tool call for this request.

options.title: Document as unsupported
options.body: Keep current runtime behavior and document affected non-native providers as unreliable for tool-enabled agents.

recommendation.title: Detect and recover without execution
recommendation.body: Treat bare markers as malformed tool intent, suppress the raw marker, and retry or fall through to a tool-capable model with a clear diagnostic.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the current tool-call repair wrapper work and is the best available owner for the provider/runtime policy choice.
